variables.want: {% set s = trigger.to_state.state %}{% set a = states('alarm_control_panel.home') %}{% if s == 'on' and a in ['armed_home', 'disarmed'] %}night{% elif s == 'off' and a == 'armed_night' %}home{% else %}none{% endif %}

variables.sleep_on: {% set a = states('alarm_control_panel.home') %}{{ a == 'armed_night' or (a in ['unavailable', 'unknown'] and is_state('schedule.climate_night','on')) }}

description: The alarm is the house's day/night switch (2026-10-11, operator). alarm_control_panel.home == armed_night IS night for the climate loop, the lights (binary_sensor.lighting_night) and Adaptive Lighting's sleep mode. schedule.climate_night only moves the alarm at its EDGES: on -> Night from Home or Disarmed, off -> Home from Night. Away, Triggered and anything already there are left alone, so a manual switch wins until the next edge. Alarmo here has no sensors, codes or sirens - arming is a mode switch only. Tests: tests/climate/cases.py (House). While the alarm itself is unavailable/unknown, the schedule stands in for night (review F12) - the same rule as the climate loop and the lights.
